chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi from Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik from Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna al-Attar from Abdullah ibn Bukair from Ubayd ibn Zurarah said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'The people will lose their Imam, so he will attend the pilgrimage season; he will see them, but they will not see him.'

key_terms.الْمَوْسِم: the pilgrimage season (specifically referring to Hajj)
key_terms.يَفْقِدُ: he is lost/unseen (from the perspective of the people)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam do during the Hajj season during his occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the paradox of the Imam’s physical presence during the Hajj season while remaining spiritually veiled from the general populace, a key indicator of the Major Occultation (Ghaybat al-Kubra). It underscores the Shia belief that the Imam continues to guide the faithful invisibly, fulfilling his role as the *Hujjah* (proof of God) even when his face is not widely recognized. This concept reinforces the theological necessity of waiting (*Intizar*) and maintaining spiritual vigilance during the period of concealment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 119 - Narrated Muhammad bin Ja’far Asadi from Saad bin Abdullah from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Ishaq bin Muhammad Sairafi from Yahya bin Muthanna Attar from Abdullah bin Bukair from Ubaid bin Zurarah that he said:
I heard Abi Abdullah (a.s) say: “The Imam will be unseen by the people. Then he will witness those who come for Hajj pilgrimage. He will see them, but they will not see him.”
